description: Nutrition Add-Food root-cause fix + idempotency. Root cause (design §7.1, confirmed in code): backend nutritionService.getDay() and the nutritionCalc.FoodLogEntry interface omit mealId/mealName on read, so foods logged to a NAMED custom meal come back with null association and the client's NutritionDay.entriesForCustomMeal matches no section, making them vanish. The write path (add_food_sheet._buildEntry, food.dart toJson, foodLogUpsertSchema) already persists mealId/mealName correctly. Fix the read path, add client-supplied-id idempotency so slow-network re-taps never duplicate, and keep the Flutter invalidate-before-pop/loading/error states. Independent of the trainer layer; done first to keep the baseline green.
steps: Backend read-path fix: in backend/src/utils/nutritionCalc.ts add 'mealId?: string | null;' and 'mealName?: string | null;' to the FoodLogEntry interface (keep groupByMeal keyed by mealType). In backend/src/services/nutritionService.ts getDay() row mapping, add 'mealId: (r.mealId as string) ?? null, mealName: (r.mealName as string) ?? null' so the top-level entries[] retains the association. No write-path change.

Backend idempotency: add 'clientId: z.string().min(1).max(200).optional()' to foodLogUpsertSchema in backend/src/validators/nutritionValidators.ts. In nutritionService.addFood use 'const id = input.clientId ?? nutritionRepository.newLogId(uid);' then setLog(uid, id, ...), stripping clientId from the stored payload (it only drives the doc id). setLog already uses {merge:true}.

Backend tests: add backend/src/__tests__/nutritionService.test.ts following the userRepository.test.ts mock-Firestore pattern. Cover: (a) getDay preserves mealId/mealName; (b) totals incl. fiber/sugar/sodium; (c) duplicate clientId add writes exactly one foodLogs doc / no doubled totals.

Flutter: in frontend/lib/models/food.dart add an optional clientId field to FoodLogEntry and emit it in toJson() only when non-null. In frontend/lib/features/nutrition/presentation/widgets/add_food_sheet.dart generate one stable id in initState (e.g. DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toString()), capture dateKey at open, pass the id into the built FoodLogEntry on both selected-food and custom-food paths, and confirm _add() keeps ref.invalidate(nutritionDayProvider) before Navigator.pop(), the _saving guard, and SnackBar-on-failure.

Flutter test: add frontend/test/add_food_sheet_test.dart overriding nutritionRepositoryProvider/nutritionDayProvider with fakes — add a food to a named custom meal, refresh, assert it renders in that meal's section (entriesForCustomMeal) and daily totals include it. Follow the frontend/test/food_model_test.dart style.
acceptance_criteria: A food logged to a named custom meal is returned by getDay with mealId/mealName intact and renders in that meal's section on the client.
Meal total and daily totals (calories/protein/carbs/fat/fiber/sugar/sodium) include the added food.
Calling addFood twice with the same clientId results in exactly one foodLogs doc and no doubled totals.
Loading (spinner), success (invalidate+pop), and failure (SnackBar) states are each handled.
npm test (backend) and flutter test (frontend) pass including the new tests; existing nutritionCalc.test.ts and food_model_test.dart still pass.
verification: In backend/: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
In frontend/: flutter analyze && flutter test
findings: DONE. Backend read-path fix: nutritionCalc.FoodLogEntry gained 'mealId?: string|null' + 'mealName?: string|null'; nutritionService.getDay() now maps 'mealId'/'mealName' (defaulting null) onto top-level entries[] so named-custom-meal logs survive the round-trip. Idempotency: foodLogUpsertSchema gained optional 'clientId' (z.string().min(1).max(200)); addFood() strips clientId from the stored body and uses it as the Firestore doc id (id = input.clientId ?? newLogId), setLog is {merge:true} so a re-tap updates the same doc -> no duplicate / no doubled totals. updateFood() also strips clientId before persisting (never stored). ESLint does NOT honor underscore-prefixed unused vars, so in updateFood the discarded clientId is handled via `const {clientId, ...data} = input; void clientId;` rather than `_clientId`. Flutter: FoodLogEntry gained optional 'clientId', emitted in toJson() only when non-null (placed before mealId). add_food_sheet.dart generates one stable _clientId in initState (DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toString()) reused on every save attempt and passed into both the selected-food and custom-food FoodLogEntry; dateKey is captured at open via widget.dateKey; _add() keeps ref.invalidate(nutritionDayProvider) before Navigator.pop(), the _saving guard, and SnackBar-on-failure (all already present, confirmed). Tests: backend/src/__tests__/nutritionService.test.ts (6 tests: getDay preserves mealId/mealName, defaults to null when absent, totals incl fiber/sugar/sodium, duplicate clientId => 1 doc / no doubled totals, clientId not persisted, distinct ids when no clientId). frontend/test/add_food_sheet_test.dart (2 tests: pumps AddFoodSheet, fills custom form, taps Add food, asserts one write with mealId/mealName/clientId; and entriesForCustomMeal renders it with totals). Verification ALL GREEN: backend npm run typecheck + npm run lint + npm test (17 files, 100 tests pass); frontend flutter analyze (no issues) + flutter test (all pass). NOTE for later steps reusing nutrition for the trainer read-only view: getDay now returns mealId/mealName on each entry, and the Flutter FoodLogEntry/clientId is write-only (never read back from server).
